BETWEEN:-
 NITESH HARIJAN, S/O SHRI GOVERDHAN HARIJAN,
AGED ABOUT 24 YEARS

, OCCUPATION: LABOUR R/O  WARD NO.5, NEAR KALI MANDIR KHALESAR, UMARIA  P.S.UMARIA DISTRICT UMARIYA (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI RAJENDRA YADAV - ADVOCATE)
 AND

THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH  P.S.KOTWALI UMARIYA DISTRICT-UMARIYA (MADHYA  PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI HIMANSHU TIWARI - PANEL LAWYER)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER

This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.145/2023, dated 26.03.2023, registered at Police Station - Kotwali, District Umariya (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n) and 506 of IPC.

Applicant is in detention since 27.03.2023.
2.
As per the prosecution story, on 26.03.2023, 26 years old prosecutrix submitted an application in writing before police alleging that she was married to her deceased husband in the year 2012.
She is blessed with a six years old son.
Her husband has died.
After the death of her husband, she was working as a compounder in R.K. Hospital, Umariya and there she met with Nitesh sweeper who assured her to keep her as wife and to give his name to her son.
On 15.08.2016, he committed rape upon her and thereafter, repeatedly raped her for so many years.
On 26.02.2023, Nitesh again raped her but refused to marry her.
FIR was registered.
After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
He is only 24 years old young boy.
Prosecutrix is pressurizing her to marry with him.
He never raped her.
He had no physical relation with her.
Applicant and prosecutrix both are major.
Applicant is 2 years younger to prosecutrix.
After investigation charge sheet has been filed.
Trial of the case will take considerable time.
Therefore, it has been prayed that applicant be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant.

5. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and material available on record, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre trial detention of the applicant is not warranted.
Consequently, first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant - Nitesh Harijan be released on bail on h is furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case o f bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
8. Certified copy as per rules.
(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE Jasleen Nitesh Harijan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135186672/
